newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer gets prison for obstructing SEC probe.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer gets prison for obstructing SEC probe.

text.p: A Florida lawyer was sentenced to five months in prison Thursday for obstructing Securities and Exchange proceedings by withholding damaging tapes about the target of an SEC probe.

The lawyer, Lloyd Schwed, 34, of Jupiter, Fla., was also sentenced to five months of home confinement by U.S. District Judge Harold Baer in Manhattan federal court. Schwed previously pleaded guilty to the obstruction charge.

Prosecutors said Schwed had represented several clients in National Association of Securities Dealers arbitration proceedings against the target of the SEC probe. The lawyer said he had tapes that were damaging to the target and the SEC subpoenaed the recordings.
Schwed was charged with telling the target that if he settled certain cases with his clients, he would not turn over the tapes to the SEC.

Schwed demanded $1.45 million from the target to settle the cases. In exchange, the lawyer said he would destroy the damaging tapes. Schwed expected to receive one-third of any money received by his clients as a contingency fee.
